correctness.rationale: Exact residual-parametrization follows from polynomial divisibility by the two coordinate factors; coefficient row/column constraints are equivalent to unit-flow conservation. Lower bound uses Cauchy--Schwarz on 2L axis coefficients and minimizes one complex quadratic. Upper bound constructs every coefficient by consecutive blocks of width floor sqrt L, checks i+j<=L, exact row/column sums and energy 2/M+K/M^2. Squared tensor projection gives the rectangular comparison. The inequalities imply n E_n->2 and an O(n^-3/2) difference. Code independently checks the Gram matrix, graph and polynomial quotient with exact Fractions for n=0,...,7; these tests do not replace the infinite argument.

value.rationale: The product (1-z)(1-w) is a natural crossing of two boundary zero divisors, explicitly investigated for cyclicity and nonoptimal approximants in the 2015 primary literature. The new quantity is the best error under the geometrically natural total-degree cutoff, not an arbitrary numerical slice. Its previously undetermined leading constant 2 is matched by rigorous universal lower and constructive upper bounds. The result quantifies the approximation complexity at this crossing, relates a two-variable analytic extremal problem to electrical network geometry, and proves that the coupled total-degree cutoff loses only O(n^-3/2) squared error relative to the much larger rectangular-degree cutoff.
